title: Choose Bork's dark-mode composition
question: The visual world is fixed: a polished, familiar social feed. Choose the composition the implementation should match.

options.label: Balanced Shell
options.lineage: dark social app shell with a high-contrast reading column
options.thesis: A conventional three-column frame makes every social affordance immediately recognizable.
options.viewport: Navigation, centered timeline, and a quiet context rail share the viewport; the light feed column carries maximum contrast.
options.risk: The white timeline is brighter and more Twitter-like than the requested dark-first presentation.

options.label: Night Rails
options.lineage: one continuous midnight app with three purposeful rails
options.thesis: Navigation, the live feed, and honest project proof each get a clear lane without breaking the dark canvas.
options.viewport: A compact navigation and sign-in rail, broad feed lane, and small Built by Colton rail fill the first viewport.
options.risk: The right rail must remain concise or it will read like a portfolio sidebar instead of product context.

options.label: Focus Lane
options.lineage: a narrow utility rail and one uninterrupted feed
options.thesis: Bork puts almost all visual weight on writing and reading, with personality carried by dogs, copy, and one blue action.
options.viewport: A narrow left rail supports a generous integrated composer and four border-separated posts; the right side stays mostly quiet.
options.risk: The restraint leaves fewer places to explain the engineering at first glance.
